breakfast.name: Oil Down (Breadfruit Stew)
instructions: Layer breadfruit, meats, callaloo in pot
Add coconut milk and spices
Cook until coconut milk 'oils down'
Add dumplings last 15 min
breakfast.description: Grenada's national dish — one-pot breadfruit stew in coconut.

breakfast.name: Cocoa Tea
instructions: Grate cocoa ball into boiling water
Add spices, simmer 5 min
Add milk and sugar
Strain and grate fresh nutmeg on top
breakfast.description: Rich cocoa drink from Grenada's own cocoa and nutmeg.

breakfast.name: Oil Down (Grenada's National Dish)
instructions: Soak salted meat overnight to reduce salt
Layer in a large pot: salted meat and chicken on the bottom
Add breadfruit cubes, dumplings
Pour coconut milk over everything — enough to cover
Add turmeric (turns everything golden), thyme, garlic, Scotch bonnet, onion
Cover tightly, simmer on low heat for 1+ hours
Do NOT stir — the layers cook together as the coconut milk reduces
The coconut milk 'oils down' — reduces until the fat coats everything and the bottom caramelizes
The bottom layer (the bun-bun) is the most prized part — crispy, caramelized coconut-meat
Serve from the pot — everyone gathers around with a plate
breakfast.description: Grenada's national dish — breadfruit, meat, and dumplings slow-cooked in coconut milk until the milk 'oils down' into a rich, golden, caramelized coating. The bottom layer (bun-bun) is the most fought-over part. Oil Down is made communally, eaten communally, and the 'oil down' reduction concept has gone viral as one of the Caribbean's most unique cooking techniques.

breakfast.name: Cocoa Tea (Grenadian Hot Chocolate)
ingredients: Cocoa balls (Grenadian — made from locally grown cacao, roasted, ground with spices and shaped into balls)
Nutmeg (freshly grated — Grenada is the Isle of Spice)
instructions: Grate cocoa ball into hot milk or water
Whisk vigorously as it heats — it must be frothy
Add sugar, cinnamon, bay leaf
Simmer 10 min until thick and rich
Grate fresh Grenadian nutmeg on top — the finishing touch
The cocoa balls are handmade: cacao beans roasted, ground, mixed with spices, rolled into balls
Grenada grows both cacao and nutmeg — two tropical luxuries from one tiny island
This is Grenadian morning — rich chocolate from the tree down the road
breakfast.description: Hot chocolate from the source — Grenada grows its own cacao AND is the world's second-largest nutmeg producer. Grated cocoa balls simmered in milk with freshly grated nutmeg. The 'bean-to-cup on a tiny Caribbean island' story and the Isle of Spice origin make Grenadian cocoa tea endlessly viral.

lunch.name: Lambi (Conch) Curry
instructions: Dice conch, tenderize
Sauté onion, garlic, curry
Add coconut milk and potatoes
Add conch, simmer 25 min

lunch.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Boil callaloo and dasheen
Add coconut milk, okra, crab
Season with thyme and pepper
Simmer until thick

lunch.name: Lambi (Conch) Curry
instructions: Tenderize conch by scoring and pounding — it's tough if not properly prepared
Cut into bite-sized pieces
Sauté onion, garlic, add curry powder — fry until fragrant
Add conch, cook briefly
Add coconut milk and potatoes
Simmer 25-30 min until conch is tender and sauce is thick
Add Scotch bonnet and thyme
Serve over rice
The curry-coconut combination with the firm-textured conch is uniquely Caribbean
lunch.description: Grenadian conch curry — tender lambi in a coconut-curry sauce fragrant with Grenada's homegrown spices. The Caribbean-Indian fusion (curry traditions brought by Indian workers) creates something unique to the islands. The conch-tenderizing technique and the spice-island story are viral Caribbean food content.

lunch.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Cook callaloo leaves until very soft
Add okra — the sliminess helps thicken the soup
Add coconut milk, crab or salt meat
Simmer until thick and green
Add dumplings to cook in the soup if desired
Season with Scotch bonnet, thyme, garlic
The soup should be thick, green, and rich with coconut
Serve hot — this is Caribbean green comfort in a bowl
lunch.description: Grenada's thick green soup — callaloo leaves simmered with coconut milk, okra, and crab into a deeply green, thick, nourishing bowl. The Caribbean's answer to spinach soup but infinitely richer. The vibrant green color and the coconut richness make callaloo soup viral Caribbean comfort food.

lunch.name: Stewed Fish with Green Banana
instructions: Season fish with lime, salt, pepper — marinate 20 min
Brown fish on both sides in oil, set aside
Sauté onion, garlic, thyme, tomato paste
Add water, bring to simmer, add green bananas
Cook bananas 15 min until tender
Return fish to pot, simmer 10 min in sauce
Add Scotch bonnet for heat
Serve fish on banana with sauce ladled over
lunch.description: Grenadian stewed fish served over boiled green banana — the islands' everyday protein-and-provision lunch. The whole fish simmered in a tomato-herb sauce is quintessential Caribbean home cooking.

dinner.name: Stew Fish Grenadian
instructions: Season fish with lime and green seasoning
Fry lightly
Make sauce with tomatoes, onion, garlic, thyme
Smother fish in sauce
dinner.description: Pan-fried fish in Grenadian Creole sauce.

dinner.name: Nutmeg Chicken
instructions: Marinate chicken with nutmeg, garlic, ginger, soy, honey, lime
Roast at 190°C 35 min until golden
Grate more fresh nutmeg on top
dinner.description: Roasted chicken glazed with Grenada's famous nutmeg.

dinner.name: Jerk Chicken Grenadian Style
ingredients: Jerk marinade: Scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, green onion, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, lime juice, nutmeg, cinnamon
instructions: Blend all jerk spices into a thick paste
The allspice and nutmeg are heavier in Grenadian jerk — the Isle of Spice influence
Marinate chicken overnight — minimum 4 hours
Grill over charcoal (pimento wood if available) — low and slow
Turn frequently, basting with extra marinade
The skin should be charred, the meat juicy and infused with spice
Alternatively bake at 190°C for 35-40 min if no grill
Serve with rice and provisions (root vegetables)
Grenadian jerk has more nutmeg and cinnamon than Jamaican — the spice island twist
dinner.description: Grenada's take on jerk chicken — heavier on nutmeg and cinnamon than the Jamaican version, because Grenada literally grows these spices. The Isle of Spice twist on Caribbean jerk and the charcoal-grilling technique make Grenadian jerk a unique entry in the jerk-chicken viral genre.

dinner.name: Nutmeg Ice Cream
instructions: Heat cream and milk with grated nutmeg — steep 30 min
Whisk yolks with sugar
Temper hot cream into yolks, return to pot
Cook custard to 82°C, stirring constantly — do not scramble
Strain, add vanilla and salt
Chill completely, churn in ice cream maker
The nutmeg flavor should be warm and prominent — not subtle
Grenada produces the world's most aromatic nutmeg — the ice cream proves it
Serve with extra grated nutmeg on top
dinner.description: Ice cream made with the world's best nutmeg — from Grenada, the Isle of Spice. The warm nutmeg flavor in cold cream is unexpectedly perfect. Nutmeg ice cream has gone viral as a 'why didn't we think of this before' flavor, and the Grenadian origin story makes it even better.

dinner.name: Pelau (One-Pot Rice)
ingredients: Ketchup (secret ingredient in many Grenadian versions)
instructions: Caramelize brown sugar in pot until dark — 'browning' the base
Add chicken, turn in the caramel until coated and browned
Add onion, garlic, thyme, pimento
Add pigeon peas, coconut milk, water
Add rice, stir once, cover tightly
Cook on low 25-30 min — do NOT lift the lid
The coconut milk makes the rice creamy, the caramel adds color and depth
Serve from the pot — the bottom layer (bun-bun) is the prize
dinner.description: Grenada's one-pot rice — chicken browned in caramelized sugar, cooked with pigeon peas and rice in coconut milk. The caramel-browning step is the Caribbean technique that makes pelau different from every other rice dish.

dinner.name: Grilled Lobster with Nutmeg Butter
instructions: Split lobster tails lengthwise
Make nutmeg butter: soften butter, mix with grated nutmeg, garlic, lime juice, parsley
Spread nutmeg butter generously over lobster meat
Grill shell-side down first 5 min, flip, grill meat-side 3-4 min
Baste with more nutmeg butter while grilling
The nutmeg-butter melts into the lobster — warm spice meets sweet shellfish
Serve with lime wedges and grilled bread for the butter
Grenada: where lobster meets the world's best nutmeg
dinner.description: Caribbean spiny lobster grilled with Grenadian nutmeg butter — the Isle of Spice meets the sea. The warm nutmeg compound butter melting into sweet lobster is a combination only Grenada could invent. This crossover of luxury and terroir is viral seafood content.

snacks.name: Nutmeg Ice Cream
instructions: Heat milk with sugar
Add grated nutmeg generously
Cool, add cream and vanilla
Churn in ice cream maker
snacks.description: Creamy ice cream loaded with fresh Grenadian nutmeg.

snacks.name: Doubles (Street Snack)
ingredients: Bara (fried bread): flour, turmeric, cumin, yeast, water
Channa (curried chickpeas): chickpeas, curry powder, cumin, garlic, Scotch bonnet
instructions: Make bara dough with turmeric and cumin — let rise
Fry small rounds until puffed and golden
Make channa: curry chickpeas with garlic, cumin, Scotch bonnet — slightly saucy
To assemble: two bara, spoonful of channa, tamarind sauce, cucumber chutney, pepper sauce
Fold and eat with hands — it's messy and perfect
The name 'doubles' = two bara
Every Caribbean island has its own doubles vendor — Grenada's version has more spice
snacks.description: Two pieces of fried turmeric bread sandwiching curried chickpeas with tamarind and pepper sauce — the Caribbean's most perfect street food. Grenada's version gets extra spice from the island's own nutmeg and pepper. The messy, flavorful, cheap perfection of doubles is perpetually viral.

snacks.name: Nutmeg Syrup (for Everything)
instructions: Make simple syrup: sugar and water, simmer until dissolved
Add generous amount of freshly grated nutmeg
Add lime juice
Simmer 10 min until fragrant
Strain or leave the nutmeg in
Use on pancakes, ice cream, in cocktails, over fruit, in tea
This is the Isle of Spice's universal condiment
The warm-sweet-citrus flavor profile works on literally everything
snacks.description: Grenada's universal condiment — freshly grated nutmeg simmered into a sweet syrup that goes on everything from pancakes to cocktails. When your island produces the world's best nutmeg, you put it in everything. The versatility and the spice-island origin story are viral.

snacks.name: Tamarind Balls
instructions: Extract tamarind pulp from pods, remove seeds
Mix pulp with sugar — taste and adjust, should be sweet-sour-tangy
Add a tiny bit of salt to enhance flavors
Add hot pepper if you want the spicy version
Roll into small balls
Coat in extra sugar if desired
Let set at room temperature
The sweet-sour-spicy hit is addictive — you cannot eat just one
These are sold at every school, every roadside, every beach in Grenada
snacks.description: Caribbean tamarind balls — sweet, sour, sometimes spicy, always addictive. Rolled by hand from fresh tamarind pulp and sugar. Sold everywhere in Grenada — school gates, beaches, market stalls. The simple tangy-sweet profile has made tamarind balls viral Caribbean snack content.

snacks.name: Fried Plantain (Sweet)
ingredients: Ripe plantains (very yellow with black spots — the riper the sweeter)
instructions: Peel ripe plantains, slice diagonally — about 1cm thick
Heat oil in a pan — medium heat
Fry slices until golden brown on each side — 2-3 min per side
The natural sugars caramelize — the edges should be dark and crispy
Drain briefly, sprinkle with salt — the salt-sweet contrast is key
Optional: dust with cinnamon
These are the Caribbean's universal side dish — served with everything
snacks.description: Sweet fried plantain — the Caribbean's universal side dish. Ripe plantain sliced and fried until the natural sugars caramelize into golden, crispy-edged, sweet perfection. Every Caribbean island, every meal, every table.

desserts.name: Sweet Potato Pudding
instructions: Mix grated sweet potato with coconut milk, sugar, spices
Add raisins and butter
Pour into greased pan
Bake at 160°C 60 min

desserts.name: Nutmeg Rum Cake
ingredients: Dark rum (Grenadian — Clarke's Court or Westerhall)
instructions: Soak dried fruit in rum overnight (or longer — weeks is better)
Cream butter and sugar, add eggs
Add flour, baking powder, nutmeg, cinnamon, vanilla
Fold in rum-soaked fruit and the soaking rum
Pour into greased bundt pan
Bake at 160°C for 40-45 min until a skewer comes out clean
While warm, poke holes and pour more rum over the cake
The cake should be dense, moist, and boozy
The nutmeg is what makes this Grenadian and not just 'rum cake'
Ages beautifully — even better after a few days
desserts.description: Grenada's legendary rum cake — dark rum and freshly grated nutmeg in a dense, boozy, fruit-studded cake. The island produces both the rum and the nutmeg, making this a true terroir dessert. The 'pour more rum on it' step and the nutmeg-forward spicing make Grenadian rum cake viral in the Caribbean baking genre.

desserts.name: Coconut Sugar Cake
instructions: Grate fresh coconut
Make syrup: sugar and water, boil until thick
Add grated coconut and ginger
Stir constantly until mixture pulls away from pot and is thick
Add pink food coloring (traditional but optional)
Drop spoonfuls onto wax paper or banana leaf
Let cool and harden — they become chewy-crunchy
The ginger heat and coconut sweetness are the signature combination
These are the candy of the Caribbean — every child's after-school treat
desserts.description: Caribbean coconut sugar cake — grated coconut cooked in sugar syrup with ginger until it sets into pink, chewy-crunchy candy drops. The traditional pink color, the ginger bite, and the coconut chew make sugar cake the Caribbean's most nostalgic confection.

drinks.name: Rum Punch
instructions: Mix rum, juices, grenadine, bitters
Serve over ice
Grate fresh nutmeg on top
drinks.description: Grenadian rum punch with freshly grated nutmeg.

drinks.name: Seamoss Drink
instructions: Boil soaked sea moss until dissolved
Blend with milk, sugar, spices
Chill and serve

drinks.name: Rum Punch (Grenadian)
instructions: The Caribbean rum punch formula: 1 sour, 2 sweet, 3 strong, 4 weak
Mix lime juice (sour), syrup (sweet), rum (strong), ice/water (weak)
Add a generous dash of Angostura bitters
Stir well with ice
Grate fresh Grenadian nutmeg on top — the defining Grenadian touch
The nutmeg on rum punch is how you know you're in Grenada
Serve cold — this is the drink of every lime, every beach, every fête
drinks.description: Grenadian rum punch — the classic Caribbean formula (1 sour, 2 sweet, 3 strong, 4 weak) finished with freshly grated Grenadian nutmeg. The nutmeg on top is the Isle of Spice's signature on the Caribbean's national cocktail.

drinks.name: Seamoss Drink
instructions: Soak sea moss overnight — it expands and softens
Boil soaked sea moss until it dissolves into a gel
Blend with condensed milk, evaporated milk, nutmeg, cinnamon, vanilla
Strain if desired — some like it smooth, some like it textured
Chill — serve very cold
The texture is thick and creamy — almost like a milkshake
Sea moss is rich in minerals — it's a traditional health drink
In the Caribbean, sea moss drinks are also considered an aphrodisiac
drinks.description: Grenadian sea moss drink — dried sea moss boiled to a gel, blended with condensed milk, nutmeg, and cinnamon into a thick, creamy, mineral-rich shake. The health benefits (92 of 102 minerals the body needs) and the Caribbean aphrodisiac reputation make sea moss drinks perpetually viral.
